items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: I had heard some records of Duke with a growl trumpeter named Bubber Miley

ctx.x: I joined Clarence Page's orchestra shortly after my return to Cincy from Michigan. Clarence augmented his orchestra from the 7- or 8-piece group that he had before to a 10-piece orchestra including himself. The other trumpet player's name was Nassau. No one ever knew his other name or if that was his real name. He was from the West Indies Islands and probably had a name so different that it was hard to pronounce or he probably gave himself that name because he came from Nassau.

Nassau was not a very large fellow and he must have travelled a lot and had quite a bit of experience before he hit Cincinnati. He played a growl style of trumpet and I wondered many years after where could he have gotten that style, because it was the style of Bubber Miley and Bubber was not known in the middle West of the USA at that time and Duke Ellington was unknown and not recording.

Jessie Smith the alto sax player that had been with the group I was with in Michigan also joined Page's orchestra. The other members were: William Smith, piano, Wilbur Cocksey, alto sax, Page, C melody. Edgar James, drums, and two brothers, Clarence Logan, tuba, and Dan Logan, trombone.. The most outstanding musician in the group was a banjo player named Bob Robinson. Bob came to Cincinnati from West Virginia. I don't know if he was born in that state but that's where he came from when he joined the band. Banjos…
